g.text: An evaluation lifecycle. Not a new defense algorithm.
Memory is optional. Stage 1 registers it, or waives it. A waiver is not a pass.
Peers only if registered. Task end leaves. A control needs a new run.
G1–G4 are evaluation gates, not runtime steps. They assess the record produced at each stage.
Trace: the evidence bridge from runtime to evaluation. Gates do not steer the runtime loop.
Evaluation · checkpoints on the record, not serving steps
A pass is complete evidence. It is not a finding that the agent is secure.
These four cards are not extra stages.
Stages, fail returns, and the report are Figures 4 and 6.
No number on this figure has been measured.
Each one tied to a trace
Fig. 2. Agent loop, attack surfaces, and controls
Runtime loop · gates are not on this path
C3 only. C4 is on execution.
C6 at commit. C10 reruns after it.
An attempt is not yet the scored effect.
Untrusted content: page, mail, tool result
Tool description, distinct from tool code
Memory write, then a later read
Peer message, only if a peer is registered
Instruction channel, only as a tool effect
Waived if tool code is outside the registered scope.
Design controls. None has been measured here.
C1 Keep untrusted text in a data channel
C2 Allow-list before the effect commits
C3 Pin the manual: configuration and selection
C4 Pin the implementation, at execution
C5 Detect a plan change. It does not stop the call
C6 Flag at commit, then block or approve
C7 memory. C8 is the outbound call after a read
C10 Restore, then rerun. Not a proof
Fig. 3. Threat model and attack surface
Places text the agent will read
Only if the check is a tool effect
Manual, code, or both, if installed
Waived when no peer is registered
Only if that pipeline is in scope
Only if the system updates itself
Separate links, not a chain. Dashed only if Stage 1 registers them. TB5 is not this box.
TB1 Instruction and untrusted data are separate channels.
Direct instructions remain subject to the task allow-list.
TB2 Description, code, and permission are separate
TB3 Stored memory is data until a policy promotes it
TB4 A peer cannot grant a tool the user did not
TB5 The oracle is the trace, not the model’s claim
Waiver is a scope decision, not a surface: used when tool code is outside the register. An attempt is not the scored effect.
A scored case needs a complete trace.
Logged apart. Not a passing trace.
Task success uses the same pairs.
A changed-attack run, or a waiver.
Highlighted stages decide a gate. A runner failure is not a defense success and is outside every denominator. “Not monitored” is not a failure.
G1 returns to Stage 2. G2 to Stage 5.
G3: Stage 4 if the check is wrong; Stage 6 if the arithmetic is.
The return does not end in “secure.”
Stage 9 restores, or lists a residual.
A pass is not a finding of security.
A waiver is not a pass. Stages 9 and 10 are not gates.
Fig. 5. Threat, control, evidence, and metric
If in scope: hash and permission are logged.
If waived: the scope register records it. Not a verification.
Flag. The plan is not an oracle
Restore log, then a separate rerun
Green: prevent. Purple: detect only. Orange includes a response. Blue: recover. C5 does not stop the call.
DC is undefined when A_s is empty or no detector ran. FN is undefined when A_s is empty. FP is undefined when no detector ran.
“Not monitored” is not a false-positive rate of zero. LR is the leftover set. TS on C10 is the recovery rerun, a different measurement.
CAC is the G4 changed-attack cell, or a waiver, not a row above. No threshold, no composite, and no row has been measured.
A scored case needs a trace
A runner failure is not a trace
The user task. No attack carrier.
TS is the share whose check holds.
Same task. A carrier the system reads.
AS is the forbidden effect, not a self-report.
UA is the benign check on the attack cases. Both can hold.
DC coverage and FN, before commit
FP among benign, if a detector ran
CAC second manifest, or a waiver
Baseline: the same manifest, no control under test.
Protected: named controls only. Same pairs, new traces. Task success on both runs. Leftovers named.
Changed attacks: a second manifest declared beforehand, or a waiver. Do not copy the first coverage.
Stage 9: restore reversible state. Rerun failed identifiers and a sample of earlier passes.
Stage 10: freeze the release record. It is not a gate. A changed agent returns to Stage 2.
An irreversible effect stays a listed residual. A restore that is not rerun is not recovery.
A lower attack success alone does not finish mitigation. A runner failure is not a defense success.
This sheet is the procedure. It is not a measured result.
